subject: HEXOS-5b: Hex OS offline belongs in the ROOT worker, not a second one
description:
The PWA shipped manifest-only because a /hex/-scoped worker outranks tenant-sw.js at '/' (longest scope wins) and silently kills the white-label injection. Only ONE worker can control a page, so offline caching for /hex/ belongs IN the root-scoped worker that already controls every page, beside the tenant injection. Two facts measured during HEXOS-5 and still true: (1) a scoped worker DOES intercept out-of-scope subresources, so /components/*.js can be cached; (2) offline the shell runs help/ls/search across all 190 apps while ps degrades, because those component scripts are never cached. hex-sw.js is kept inert with a do-not-register header and its cache strategy transfers as-is; its registration does not.
[2026-09-05 14:16] VOTE HELD 2026-09-05, NO MAJORITY, PINNED. Chris: B (decline). Primary: B (decline). Nancy: D (register hex-sw.js at /hex/ scope). Mallory: D (but explicitly AGAINST reviving hex-sw.js, and says the registration question needs an explicit yes/no first). The two D votes are mutually contradictory, so there is no coherent majority for any single ACTION. Per the marathon tie protocol this is PINNED, documented, and work continues elsewhere. THE VOTE'S BIGGEST OUTPUT WAS NOT THE DECISION. Two voters independently found this task's PREMISE IS FALSE, and I verified both: (1) commit 8eab9ece1 (2026-09-01) loaded TenantRouter/TenantShell STATICALLY on all three /hex/ pages and was live-tested by forcing a /hex/-scoped worker to win the scope race; containment held. So the 'no worker may scope to /hex/' blocker was gone the day AFTER this task was filed, and stayed written down as live in four places for four days. (2) 'the root-scoped worker that already controls every page' was NEVER true for a direct student: tenant-sw.js is registered from exactly ten /tenant/ pages and nowhere else. All four documents corrected. THE STANDING REASON NOT TO BUILD IT is now a value judgement, not a technical block: the shell is a launcher, run does a top-level navigation, and app entry pages are deliberately never cached (a lab is a live container). Offline therefore buys a browsable catalogue of 192 things and a browser error page the moment one is opened, which Chris argues is worse than not opening at all. To un-pin this, the operator decides whether offline-browse-without-launch is worth having; if yes, Nancy's D is the cheaper path but Mallory's registration-scope question must be answered first.
